description: Establish the baseline, produce the audit + migration map, then implement redesign steps 1-2: marketing design tokens and the new minimal sticky navigation with a Product mega-menu. This is the foundation every later feature builds on. Verify the existing build/tests are green FIRST so any later breakage is attributable. All work is on the PUBLIC marketing site only; do not touch authenticated app routes/components.
steps: Confirm the baseline is green before editing anything: cd /projects/sandbox/AmazAI/web && export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && . /root/.nvm/nvm.sh && npm run build (must be clean) && npm test (expect 28 files / 194 tests passing). If not green, stop and report.

Write the audit + migration map to /projects/sandbox/AmazAI/.agents/tasks/task-marketing-site-redesign/MIGRATION_MAP.md. Trace the ACTUAL code (do not guess) and produce a keep/modify/replace table covering: current routes (web/src/main.jsx Router + PUBLIC_PATHS + theme.js PUBLIC regex + index.html before-paint regex), shared layout (PublicShell), header (PublicShell TopNav), footer (PublicShell PublicFooter), typography + design tokens (styles.css :root and the two dark blocks; premium.css; theme.js), existing marketing components/screens (screens/marketing/*.jsx, Landing.jsx), responsive breakpoints (grep @media in styles.css), existing product screenshots/components reusable as marketing visuals (Companion system, Room/Rooms/Sections/Composer/PresenceFeed/CoordinationFeed/Delegation/Handoff/ApprovalCard/ConnectionBar/Cards/AgentAvatar/AgentProfile), signup/sign-in routes (auth0.jsx startLogin), analytics (search the repo; note if none exists), SEO metadata (Seo.jsx + index.html), and pricing source (marketing/Pricing.jsx + Pricing.test.jsx). For each row state keep/modify/replace and one-line rationale.

STEP 1 (marketing design tokens): In web/src/styles.css, ADD an additive, marketing-scoped token layer + primitives. Do NOT change the shared app tokens' meaning or the dark-mode blocks. Scope marketing tokens under a wrapper class (e.g. `.mkt` applied to the marketing root) or as new --mkt-* variables so the authenticated app theme is unaffected. Establish: white primary canvas (#fff), near-black ink for type, subtle neutral borders/hairlines, a selective AmazAI purple accent (reuse existing brand purples --brand-3 #8b2fe0 / --brand-4 #c026d3 and the accent blue), responsive fluid type scale using clamp() for hero/section headings (large editorial hero, strong headline/body contrast, readable line-lengths ~60ch, generous vertical rhythm), and spacing tokens. Keep body text NOT oversized. Provide reusable section/container primitives (max-width container, section padding, eyebrow, kicker, section-title, lede). Since the public site is forced light by theme.js, these tokens only need a light definition.

STEP 2 (navigation): Rewrite the exported TopNav in web/src/components/PublicShell.jsx as a minimal sticky top nav. Left: AmazAI Logo (link to /welcome-to-amazai). Center primary nav: Product, Solutions, Resources, Pricing. Right: `Sign in` (ghost, startLogin(loginWithRedirect,{returnTo:'/'})) and `Start free` (primary, startLogin(loginWithRedirect,{signup:true,returnTo:'/welcome'})). The `Product` item opens a structured mega-menu with three groups: WORK (Companions, Rooms, Routines, Artifacts), CONNECT (Connectors, Browser & Computer, Developer Tools), DISCOVER (Unified Inbox, Search, Templates). Mega-menu links should point to on-page anchors on the homepage where those sections exist (e.g. /welcome-to-amazai#companions) or to existing routes where sensible; items without a destination yet may be plain non-navigating labels or point to the closest existing page - do NOT invent new routes/pages. Solutions/Resources can be simple links (Solutions -> /use-cases or a homepage anchor; Resources -> keep a small dropdown or link to /faq). Keep the default nav extremely restrained. Sticky positioning, closes menu on route change and outside click (preserve existing useEffect patterns), keyboard-accessible (aria-expanded, focusable trigger, Escape to close), and no horizontal overflow. Do not break existing routes; the nav renders on every public page via PublicShell and Landing.
Add the CSS for the sticky nav + mega-menu to styles.css under the marketing token layer. Ensure it works over the white canvas with a subtle hairline border and a compact height.
Re-run build and tests; keep them green. If Landing.jsx or any marketing screen references removed nav internals, update call sites.
acceptance_criteria: MIGRATION_MAP.md exists at the task dir and contains a keep/modify/replace row for every item listed in the user's 'Before coding' audit list, each grounded in a real file path.

web/src/styles.css contains a marketing-scoped token/primitive layer (white canvas, near-black ink, neutral borders, selective purple accent, clamp-based fluid type scale) that does NOT alter the authenticated app's existing token values or dark blocks.

TopNav renders a sticky minimal nav with Product / Solutions / Resources / Pricing and Sign in / Start free, and Product opens a mega-menu with the WORK/CONNECT/DISCOVER groups and exact item labels from the spec.
Sign in and Start free call startLogin with the correct options (returnTo '/' for sign in; signup:true returnTo '/welcome' for start free).
npm run build is clean and npm test passes (>=194 tests) after the changes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/AmazAI/web && export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && . /root/.nvm/nvm.sh && npm run build
Confirm MIGRATION_MAP.md exists and covers all audit items.
findings:
Baseline confirmed green before edits: clean vite build + 28 files/194 tests. Still green after changes (194 passing).

DELIVERED:
- MIGRATION_MAP.md written at the task dir with a keep/modify/replace row for every audit item (routes+3 mirrors, PublicShell, TopNav, footer, typography, tokens+2 dark blocks, premium.css, marketing screens/Landing, breakpoints, Companion/product surfaces, auth0 startLogin, analytics[none found], Seo.jsx+index.html, Pricing source, Logo).
- STEP 1 tokens: additive marketing layer appended to web/src/styles.css, scoped to `.mkt, .mkt-nav` (so the sticky nav carries its own tokens even when rendered directly by Landing). White canvas, near-black ink, neutral hairlines, selective purple accent reusing --brand-3/-4/--brand-sweep, clamp() fluid type scale (hero/h2/h3/lede, body NOT oversized ~17px), spacing rhythm, and .mkt-container/.mkt-section/.mkt-eyebrow/.mkt-title/.mkt-lede primitives. Shared app tokens and both dark blocks untouched.
- STEP 2 nav: rewrote TopNav in web/src/components/PublicShell.jsx as a minimal sticky bar (.mkt-nav). Left AmazAI logo -> /welcome-to-amazai; centre Product/Solutions/Resources/Pricing; right Sign in (ghost) + Start free (primary). Product opens a mega-menu WORK[Companions,Rooms,Routines,Artifacts]/CONNECT[Connectors->/integrations, Browser & Computer, Developer Tools]/DISCOVER[Unified Inbox,Search,Templates]. Mega-menu links use on-page homepage anchors (#companions etc., sections land in FEAT-002/003) or existing routes; NO new routes created. Accessible: aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, role=menu/menuitem, Escape closes, closes on route change + outside click. Sign in -> startLogin(returnTo:'/'); Start free -> startLogin(signup:true, returnTo:'/welcome').

NOTES/DEVIATIONS:
- Solutions links to /use-cases, Resources links to /faq (simple links per spec's allowance), Pricing -> /pricing.
- Old CSS classes .public-nav*/.public-nav-dropdown* and .landing-nav-links are now unused by the nav but left in place (still referenced by nothing harmful; removing risks touching Landing which FEAT-002 replaces).
- No analytics library exists anywhere in web/ (verified by repo-wide search); recorded in the migration map for FEAT-004.
- Primary nav hides <=860px to avoid horizontal overflow; full mobile menu is a FEAT-004 concern.
- No new dependencies; CSS-only motion consistent with the Companion system.
